name: 结构性矛盾分析
purpose: Identify whether several visible problems are coupled by a shared carrier, constraint, or feedback mechanism; distinguish the structural key mechanism from the current action priority; and turn competing structures into divergent predictions and a practical test.
eligibility_checks: the decision objective and system boundary can be stated
evidence contains a plausible coupling, trade-off, feedback loop, heterogeneous response, or stage-dependent driver shift
the ordinary explanation can be preserved while a structurally different explanation is tested
a non-contradiction explanation such as measurement error, confounding, or a single-point fault can still be considered
assumptions: a contradiction is a relationship between interdependent mechanisms, not a synonym for any difference or negative metric
the dominant relationship and dominant side are scoped to a stated object, period, and decision
the structural key mechanism and the most practical next action may differ
causal strength remains limited by the underlying study design
outputs: bounded map of candidate structural tensions
concrete coupling carrier and divergent predictions versus the ordinary explanation
separate structural-key and action-priority rankings or an explicit not-applicable result
plain-language decision brief with switch conditions
diagnostics: missing shared constraint or interaction mechanism
candidate is only a relabeling of the ordinary explanation
apparent contradiction explained by aggregation, measurement, or sample composition
structural importance and action priority were conflated
insufficient evidence for a dominant relationship or stage transition
recommended next observation or low-risk test
evidence_requirements: locatable evidence for each visible phenomenon
evidence for the proposed coupling or a clearly marked mechanism hypothesis
a source-role and conflict map for multi-source evidence
at least one prediction that differs from the ordinary explanation
at least one counterexample or completed counterexample search
at least one competing non-contradiction explanation
a stated scope, stage, and condition that could reverse the conclusion
allowed_claims: a structural tension is the best-supported current explanation within a stated scope
one side currently dominates the observed result within a stated period or condition
the structurally central mechanism differs from the safest or fastest current action
the available evidence does not support a structural-contradiction interpretation
a specified observation or intervention would distinguish competing explanations
forbidden_claims: every difference, disagreement, or pair of opposing metrics is a contradiction
the largest negative contribution is automatically the primary contradiction
the easiest action or highest information-gain test is automatically the structural key mechanism
a historical analogy or theoretical quotation is evidence about the current case
a mechanism hypothesis is causal proof without an eligible design
the dominant relationship is permanent across stages or system boundaries
reader-facing reports must quote or name the intellectual source
